paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take with you, friend. The Sadducees had a clever puzzle, seven brothers and one widow, and it still missed the whole point. Jesus tells them why: "You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God." (Matthew 22:29) They knew the words well enough to build a trap out of them, but not the God behind them.

Jesus didn't just fix their math. He said that in the resurrection, people "will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven." (Matthew 22:30) The life God has coming is bigger than anything our questions can hold. Don't shrink the promise to fit your puzzle, baker.

Jesus takes them to what God said: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." He adds, "He is not the God of the dead, but of the living." (Matthew 22:32) Jesus uses those words to show that the dead do rise, because the people who belong to God are not lost to Him. So here's your hope, friend: if you belong to God, death doesn't get the last word, and no wonder the crowds were astonished at His teaching (Matthew 22:33).
